set.overview: Whaleback is a huge isolated granite fin deep in the Sequoia backcountry, and its north ridge is the classic way up it: a low fifth-class ridge climb on clean rock with plenty of exposure. The other faces are mostly third-class scrambling, so this line is the real climbing objective. The summit is tiny and airy, looking across to Glacier Ridge, Triple Divide Peak and Milestone Mountain.
set.approach: The long way in starts at the Sample Meadow trailhead and takes two days. Day one runs east about seven miles to the Sugarloaf Meadow camp, which has a bear box and a small creek. Day two continues east to the Roaring River ranger station, crosses the river and turns south up Cloud Canyon, gaining roughly 1,000 feet over about four miles to Big Wet Meadow, where the peak comes into view.

review.notes: Single publisher. Approach leg lengths stated per day, but no total to the route base and no summit-to-trailhead distance or gain, so gain and distance left out. No descent, season or second source found; descent skipped.

set.overview: North Guard is a craggy, ridge-covered peak just north of Mount Brewer, and its west ridge, called the Parapet Ridge, is an easy fifth-class ridge climb along the crest. Granite talus leads to the crest from the southwest side, and the ridge ends at a long slab-like summit block that tilts over the steep east face. It is a long, off-trail objective well beyond the end of any maintained path.
set.approach: Start at Roads End in Cedar Grove and follow the Bubbs Creek trail east, crossing several small bridges and climbing switchbacks out of the canyon to the upper bridge. Turn onto the steep Sphinx Creek trail, then leave it at the creek crossing and work cross-country through wet meadows to Sphinx Lakes. Continue over Sphinx Col, drop toward the tarn near Echo Col, and enter the drainage between North Guard and Brewer. Climb talus on the southwest side to reach the west ridge crest.
set.descent_text: Come down the way you went up. From the summit block drop into a chute, then reach a narrow class 3 crack and ramp system, and traverse back across to the drainage between North Guard and Brewer before retracing the approach out to Roads End.
hazards: Rattlesnakes on the lower Bubbs Creek trail, from Junction Meadow to the Sphinx Creek crossing
Sphinx Creek trail has rough, loose blasted-granite tread that is hard on the feet
Cross-country route-finding at Sphinx Lakes and over Sphinx Col is slow and tricky in the dark
Steep, sloping summit block above the east face

review.notes: Approach and descent from one trip report plus MP page confirming Sphinx Trail and Sphinx Lakes. MP says approach to Sphinx Lakes is over 10 miles and ~5,500 ft but that is to the lakes only and single-source, so no dist or gain set. Season not found.

set.overview: South Guard sits about a mile south of Mount Brewer on the Kings Canyon park side, its main summit at 13,232 feet. The route climbs sandy scree and sand slopes to Longley Pass, then follows the south slope to the top, with some class 3 rock just beside the sandy line near the summit. The east face drops about 3,200 feet to Lake Reflection, so the summit is a big viewpoint.
hazards: Sand and scree on the pass slopes is loose and tiring, with dislodged rocks falling down the northeast face
Early-season snow near the pass and on the slopes, so an ice axe is useful
Steep, very loose ground on the far side of Longley Pass

review.notes: Both trip reports reach Longley Pass from the east/north side of the divide, not clearly from Cedar Grove as the existing row text says, so approach and descent were skipped to avoid describing a different line. No distance, gain or season sources.

set.overview: Mount Jordan is a Kings-Kern Divide summit whose north side rises about 3,300 feet above Lake Reflection. The standard line works up an east slope of scree and talus to a notch in the north ridge, then follows the ridge with some class 3 climbing. The finish is a class 4 step across to the summit block, a move most climbers want a rope for.
set.approach: One workable way in is from the Shepherd Pass trailhead, crossing Shepherd Pass and dropping to the Kern River, then following the upper Kern to the lakes southeast of Jordan. This is a two-day approach with a camp near the big lake, and the climb itself starts from that camp up the east slope.
set.descent_text: Rappel or carefully downclimb the summit block step, then retrace the route down the north ridge and east slope of scree and talus to the lake camp. Plan on roughly three hours from summit back to a camp at the lake.
hazards: Class 4 step-across to the summit block with real exposure; a sling and rope are worth carrying
Loose scree and talus on the east slope
Lingering snow on Shepherd Pass in early summer
Little shade, so heat on the exposed slopes

review.notes: Only one trip report on a personal site describes the climb; its distance/gain figures are multi-day GPS totals so dist_km left out. Approach is one of several (others come from Cedar Grove / Sawmill Pass etc.). Season not found.

set.overview: Mount Genevra is a 13,054-foot summit on the Kings-Kern Divide, on the boundary of Kings Canyon and Sequoia national parks, first climbed by Norman Clyde in 1925. Its easiest route is class 2, so it is mainly a long remote walk and talus scramble rather than technical climbing. The north face drops about 3,000 feet toward Lake Reflection.

review.notes: No source opened gives approach, descent, distance, season or hazards for this route; skipped. Existing gain_ft left alone.

set.overview: Milestone Mountain is a 13,644-foot summit on the Great Western Divide, on the line where Sequoia and Kings Canyon national parks meet, about 0.6 miles south of Midway Mountain. Its name comes from the obelisk on its summit. The easiest route is an exposed class 3 scramble, first climbed in 1912, and it is a deep-backcountry peak that takes several days to reach.

review.notes: Wikipedia only; no approach, descent, distance, gain, season or hazard source opened. Skipped those.
